speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to narrow down the cause, how many hours old were you when the vomiting first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.

The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn with a brother who had pyloric stenosis raises the possibility of duodenal obstruction; however, the fact that the vomiting is bilious makes pyloric stenosis (which causes non-bilious vomiting) unlikely. Given the history, I need to confirm the diagnosis with an imaging study. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Series.
